newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged amid repricings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged amid repricings.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary market prices held steady Thursday in light activity, with more interest directed to the primary market's repricings.

J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. repriced Thursday's largest negotiated offering, a $399 million Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia deal. The firm lowered yields in several maturities, but left the top yield in 2020 unchanged at 5.48 percent.
Michael Davern, portfolio manager of the $127 million Nuveen Flagship Georgia Fund, said he did not participate because the deal's pricing did not meet his yield requirements.

"We just own a lot of higher yielding securities and I'd have to sell something with more yield to buy something from this bond deal at a lower yield," Davern said. "From a performance standpoint, even with the five percent coupons you don't get a very big dollar discount."

Goldman, Sachs & Co. won the day's largest competitive offering, a $40 million Kansas City, Mo., general obligation deal. The firm reoffered the 2017 term bonds at a 5.25 percent yield, and said late in the day it had an $11 million balance. Treasury prices initially firmed Wednesday after the Labor Department found an unexpected surge in jobless claims, which jumped to 377,000 in the week ended July 5 from 337,000 a week earlier.
The market retreated, however, after economists said the figure was not a sign of a weakening economy, but instead reflected expected shutdowns at car-makers as they retool to make new models.
The government long bond was unchanged at 100-25/32 to yield 6.56 percent.
In the secondary market for municipal bonds, bids on Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 rose 1/8 in late trading to 100-1/8.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2027 were bid at 5.42 percent, down one basis point.
Municipal futures for September were unchanged at 119-11/32, while September Treasury bond futures lost 1/32 to 113-28/32. The MOB spread widened to 175 ticks from 174 at the close on Wednesday.

Friday's 0830 EDT release of the Producer Price Index for June is the next major data focus for the market. Forecast call for the figure to be unchanged overall and up 0.1 percent excluding food and energy, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
